description: A fictional heavy handheld rotary rock drill game prop for a driller, chunky low-poly, held level with the drill bit forward. One big octagonal brick red-brown painted motor housing with wide chamfers. On top of the housing one thick charcoal arched carry handle running front to back on two big feet. At the rear one thick closed charcoal D-handle with a thick trigger inside. Out of the housing's left side one fat octagonal charcoal side handle sticks straight out sideways, its end open with a dark hole. On the left flank behind the side handle one big round octagonal brick red-brown gearbox cover, and ahead of it near the top one small rectangular teal lamp window in a thick raised charcoal bezel.
proportions: At the front one big cone-shaped dark steel drill bit made of three stacked steps, each step edged by one fat bright steel spiral flute ring, ending in a blunt pointed tip, about 0.45 m long and 0.30 m across its base; around the base of the bit one wide thick two-tier charcoal dust collar ring. About 1.00 m long, 0.42 m wide and 0.42 m tall. (length : width : height = 1.07 : 1 : 1.00)
sides: on the LEFT flank only: the fat side handle sticking straight out sideways (far past the housing), the round octagonal gearbox cover behind it and the teal lamp window ahead of it. The right flank is plain red-brown housing. The bit, the dust collar, the housing, the top carry handle and the rear D-handle are on the centre line, so the object is NOT symmetric: its width is mostly housing plus the side handle on the left.
